Cinnamon Churros

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 6-8 (about 20-25 churros)Prep 25 minCook 20 min

Cinnamon Churros are a beloved fried pastry, often enjoyed as a sweet treat during festive occasions in Mexico and among Mexican communities. On the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, December 12th, these crispy, sugar-dusted delights are a popular indulgence, frequently paired with a warm cup of champurrado or Mexican hot chocolate as families gather to celebrate.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) water
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 tablespoon granulated sugar (for dough)
  • 1 cup (120 g) all-purpose flour
  • 2 large eggs
  • 6 cups (1.4 L) vegetable oil, for frying
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar (for coating)
  • 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon (for coating)

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine the water, butter, salt, and 1 tablespoon of sugar. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally until the butter is fully melted.
  2. Remove the saucepan from the heat and immediately add all the flour at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
  3. Return the saucepan to low heat and continue to cook, stirring constantly for 1-2 minutes, to dry out the dough slightly. Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
  4. Transfer the dough to a large mixing bowl. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well with a wooden spoon or electric mixer after each addition until fully incorporated and the dough is smooth and glossy.
  5. Heat the vegetable oil in a large, deep pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F (175°C). Use a candy or deep-fry thermometer to monitor the temperature.
  6. While the oil heats, prepare the cinnamon sugar coating: in a shallow dish, whisk together the 1/2 cup granulated sugar and ground cinnamon.
  7. Spoon the churro dough into a piping bag fitted with a large star tip (like an Ateco 826 or 827).
  8. Carefully pipe 4-6 inch (10-15 cm) strips of dough directly into the hot oil, using kitchen shears or a knife to cut the dough from the piping bag. Do not overcrowd the pot; fry in batches.
  9. Fry the churros for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Use tongs or a slotted spoon to turn them as needed.
  10. Remove the fried churros from the oil and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil for about 30 seconds.
  11. While still warm, roll the churros in the cinnamon sugar mixture until evenly coated. Serve immediately.

Tips

  • Maintain a consistent oil temperature of 350°F (175°C) for best results; if the oil is too cool, churros will be greasy, and if too hot, they will burn outside and be raw inside.
  • For extra flavor, you can add a teaspoon of vanilla extract to the dough along with the eggs.
  • Churros are best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be reheated briefly in a toaster oven or air fryer for a few minutes until crisp again.
